newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end flat.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end flat.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Tuesday's TIFFE day session flat.
The December contract settled at 99.21, unchanged from Monday. Turnover was 17,134 contracts.

The key contract fell to an intraday low of 99.19 in the morning following a sharp rise in Tokyo stocks, but had managed to recover on short-covering as stocks' earlier gains were pared in the afternoon, traders said.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares closed up 228.38 points or 1.26 percent at 18,314.33, off an intraday high of 18,629.27.
A weak stock market is seen as positive for Euroyen futures because it underscores the need for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to maintain a low interest rate policy, traders said.

"The Euroyen futures market was following moves in stocks and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures. The December contract is likely to hover around 99.20 for the rest of this week, as people are cautious ahead of the weekend G7 meeting," said a brokerage house trader.
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita's speech in early afternoon had little impact on the market, traders said.
Matsushita told a business symposium that the strength of Japan's private-sector demand was becoming recognisable.
"The governor's economic assessment was somewhat stronger than what the bank said in its recent quarterly economic report. But he did not make clear why he was more upbeat," said a city bank trader.
The BOJ said in its quarterly economic report released in January that the economy was recovering gradually and private demand was gradually becoming more firm.
Key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.50 percent, up from 0.49 percent on Monday. The rise was due to fund shortage related to tax payments, traders said.
The BOJ injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market on Tuesday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.

About 30 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.53 percent, unchanged from Monday. Two-month CDs were issued at 0.53 percent, and then later at 0.54 percent. They were issued at 0.53 percent on Monday.
